# telemetryd

> A single-binary observability backend. OTLP in; the Loki, Tempo and Prometheus query
> APIs out. One process, one port, one data directory, no sidecars and no collector.
> Written in Rust, MIT licensed, at github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd.

Run it with `telemetryd serve` and no arguments. It listens on `127.0.0.1:4319`, stores
data beside itself, keeps 7 days of logs and traces and 30 days of metrics, and stays
under a 10 GiB disk budget. Every setting is also an environment variable named
`TELEMETRYD_<SECTION>_<KEY>`; precedence is defaults, then `telemetryd.toml`, then the
environment, then CLI flags.

## The thing most likely to mislead you

telemetryd serves the Loki, Tempo and Prometheus **APIs**, not those products. The
supported query surface is derived from what its client actually calls, so it is a
deliberate subset — writing a valid PromQL or LogQL expression is not enough for it to
run here.

Anything outside the subset is refused with HTTP 400 and a structured body naming the
construct: `{"error":{"code":"unsupported_feature","feature":"PromQL function `topk`"}}`.
The languages are parsed in full and then lowered, which is why the error can name the
function rather than reporting a syntax error.

Verified against a running instance:

- **PromQL works** for selectors and label matchers, `rate`, `increase`,
  `histogram_quantile`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `by (...)`, `without (...)`,
  `offset`, and arithmetic on a series.
- **PromQL is refused** for `topk`, `bottomk`, `quantile`, `stddev`, `irate`, `delta`,
  `absent`, and comparison operators such as `> 5`.
- **LogQL works** for stream selectors, `|=`, `!=`, `|~`, `| json` and `| logfmt`.
- **LogQL is refused** for `| line_format` and for every metric query over log streams —
  `rate`, `count_over_time`, `sum`. Use the Prometheus API for pre-aggregated metrics.
- **TraceQL works** for `{}`, attribute equality, `duration > 100ms`, `status = error`,
  `name = "..."`, and `&&` between conditions.
- **TraceQL is refused** for `||` between conditions and for `| count() > 2`.

Prefer a narrow time range on any query with a substring filter. A term that appears
nowhere is skipped without reading a segment; a term whose trigrams are individually
common — a numeric order id, say — cannot be, and the time bound is what saves the scan.

## Sending data

OTLP over HTTP with **JSON** encoding. There is no protobuf and no gRPC endpoint.

- `POST /v1/logs`, `POST /v1/traces`, `POST /v1/metrics` — OTLP/HTTP JSON
- `POST /api/v1/write` — Prometheus `remote_write` (snappy + protobuf)

`gzip`, `deflate` and `zstd` request bodies are decompressed. Records are rejected
individually and the reason is reported in OTLP's `partialSuccess` field, so a `200`
does not mean everything was stored — read the body.

The resource attribute `service.name` becomes the `app` label and severity becomes
`level`. Every other attribute is stored but is not a stream label unless listed in
`ingest.stream_labels`, which is the cardinality contract.

## Authentication

Three independent tokens guard three surfaces: `auth.ingest_token` for writes,
`auth.query_token` for the read APIs, `auth.admin_token` for `/status` and `/metrics`.
Send them as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. OIDC access tokens are accepted alongside
them when `auth.oidc.issuer` is set; scopes are not a hierarchy, so an admin scope does
not grant reads.

telemetryd refuses to start when bound to a non-loopback address with no token
configured. That is deliberate and should not be worked around with `--insecure`.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): install, run, send, query — in one read
- [Installation](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/docs/getting-started/installation.md): includes a copy-paste brief for an agent
- [Sending data](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/docs/getting-started/sending-data.md): endpoints, labels, and what a 200 does not mean
- [Docker](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/docs/getting-started/docker.md): the container, and the tokens it generates on first start
- [Configuration reference](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/docs/configuration/reference.md): every option with its default
- [COMPATIBILITY.md](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/COMPATIBILITY.md): the authoritative API subset, endpoint by endpoint
- [BUILD-STATUS.md](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/BUILD-STATUS.md): what is built, what is not, and what is deliberately absent
- [Cookbook](https://github.com/cboxdk/telemetryd/blob/main/docs/cookbook/): task-shaped recipes — relay mode, single sign-on, export and import, exposing it safely

## Do not

- Do not add an OpenTelemetry Collector. Applications send OTLP straight to telemetryd.
- Do not reach for a protobuf or gRPC OTLP exporter; neither is served.
- Do not assume an unsupported query construct is a bug. Read the `feature` field.
- Do not publish port 4319 to the internet in plain HTTP. Terminate TLS in front, or set
  `server.tls.cert_file` and `key_file`.
